newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine police block anti-Ramos protesters.
newsitem.headline: Philippine police block anti-Ramos protesters.

text.p: Philippine riot police on Monday stopped about 3,000 protesters from entering the grounds of Congress where President Fidel Ramos was due to give his last state-of-the nation address.

More than 100 police with truncheons and shields blocked the crowd of mostly workers as they marched towards the legislature demanding higher wages and an end to the economic reforms which they claim have opened up the country to foreign exploitation.
Ramos, widely praised for turning around the long-ailing Philippine economy, was to speak to Congress later in the day in what is his last year in office.

In a so far peaceful march, the demonstrators carried placards with slogans such as "Enough, enough. Let's end the Ramos regime" "Fight against imperialist globalisation" and "Enough of grinding poverty."
"We don't believe that he will step down. He has a capacity to lie," leftist leader Nathaniel Santiago told reporters.
Ramos, a former general, insists that he will quit after his one six-year term ends next June, and in a speech last Friday ruled out any chance of a second term.

But despite repeated denials, a number of Philippine commentators continue to suggest that Ramos may try to engineer another term even though it is banned by the constitution, rewritten 10 years ago after late dictator Ferdinand Marcos fled the country.

"The general (Ramos) is supposed to be singing his swan song today...but we have not counted him out. Like the cheat that he has always been, he has some aces up his sleeve," the leftist Nationalist Patriotic Alliance (Bayan) said in a statement.
"If he still fails, he may just have to do what his cousin Ferdinand Marcos did in 1972," it said, referring to Marcos's declaration of martial law.
Ramos was instrumental in the downfall of Marcos who flew from the country in 1986 after the "people's power" revolution brought Corazon Aquino to the presidency.
A further estimated 5,000 protesters gathered about four km (2.5 miles) away but police checked each group for permits, before allowing them to join the main protest group, witnesses said.
